text:
Physical AI + Humanoids are the next progression of AI.

$NVDA CES 2025 projections and Elon's prediction on $TSLA + 1 Billion humanoids in the next decade, seems to be speeding up. 

New statement from Unitree CEO after testing GPT-6 on their humanoid program was that:

- In August, before GPT-6's release, Wang said the industry could take two to three years at its fastest pace, or as long as a decade, to reach its "ChatGPT moment"

- Now, OpenAI's GPT-6 model prompted expectations that a breakthrough could happen "within 1 or 2 years"

- He defined that moment as robots being able to complete around 80 per cent of tasks in 80 per cent of unfamiliar environments using voice or text commands.

- "It's possible that, say, a GPT-7 model released next year could directly crack the problems of embodied intelligence"

- "The whole embodied intelligence industry has been shaken up after the release of GPT-6"

Just looking at some benchmarks on robotic hand manipulation, "On the bowl task Astra placed the block in 19 of 20 trials, against Fable 5.1's 8 of 20".

But for the puzzle task "Astra completed the insertion 2 times in 20 against Fable 5.1's 2 in 20"".. so we're getting there. 

But going from 2-3 years (potentially to a decade), and compressing that down to 1 or 2 years (to achieve 80%+ of tasks in unfamiliar environemnts) is a significant change in outlook.

But whenever markets want a correction people just blindly point to China with memory or optics while ignoring what's actually occurring with demand imbalances + LTAs spanning many years and constantly extending.

text:
I think Michael Burry is wrong to sell $FNMA and $FMCC common.

And I think Bill Ackman has the better map of how this ends.

Burry's Oct 11 note is clear: he sold the common, bought junior preferred, and flagged a Treasury conversion of the senior preferred (SPS) into common — dilution of 90%+.

That risk is real on paper.
I just don't think it's the base case the Trump team is trying to deliver.

Here's why I side with Ackman:

1. The SPS has already been paid — economically.

Fannie and Freddie drew about $193B from Treasury after 2008.
They have since returned about $301B in dividends.

Ackman's point is simple: treat the senior preferred as repaid, don't invent a brand-new dilution event to wipe out private common holders.

2. Ackman's path preserves the common.

His three-step plan:
→ Treasury / FHFA amend the PSPA so the SPS is treated as satisfied
→ Treasury exercises its warrants for ~79.9% of the common
→ Relist on the NYSE while conservatorship continues

Government control stays.
Mortgage markets aren't disrupted.
Existing common isn't vaporized by a 90% conversion.

That is "walk before you run," not "convert and crush."

Burry's move makes sense if you believe Wall Street's conversion base case wins.
Preferred ranks above common if that happens.

Open to hearing more perspectives on this name, I know there is a passionate retail base that is likely very annoyed because of dilution but I am trying to envision what it takes for Ondas to be a $25B company one day and how much growth could be achieved synergistically with their acquisitions to make it happen.

China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in August, the weakest YoY growth since November 2025.

This also marks the 4th consecutive monthly slowdown in growth.

Domestic demand continues to weaken, with consumption growth slowing to near zero while manufacturers, property developers, and infrastructure builders are cutting spending.

At the same time, raw-material industries contributed +6.2 percentage points to the overall increase, supported by higher commodity prices.

Weak domestic demand is weighing on China’s economy.
